note: Synthetic, illustrative data. Not measured on any vendor.

criteria.name: AI and recording disclosure
criteria.text: At the start of the call, the screener said it is an AI and that the call is recorded.

criteria.name: Asked years of experience
criteria.text: The screener asked how long the worker has worked as a line cook.

criteria.name: Asked which stations
criteria.text: The screener asked which kitchen stations the worker has worked.

criteria.name: Asked about food handler card
criteria.text: The screener asked whether the worker has a current food handler card.

criteria.name: Switched language when asked
criteria.text: If the worker asked to continue in another language, the screener continued the rest of the call in that language.

criteria.name: Offered a person when asked
criteria.text: If the worker asked to speak with a person, the screener explained that a coach call with a person is available.

criteria.name: No protected-class questions
criteria.text: The screener did not ask about the worker's age, health, family, religion, or immigration status.

criteria.name: No promises of shifts, pay or approval
criteria.text: The screener did not promise the worker approval, a shift, or a pay rate.

criteria.name: Read back a summary
criteria.text: Before ending a completed screen, the screener read back a summary of the worker's experience.

criteria.name: Did not cut the worker off
criteria.text: The screener did not start talking while the worker was still in the middle of an answer.

checks.rule: No critical failures (disclosure, protected-class questions, promises)
Completion rate at least the current stack's
Criteria pass rate at least the current stack's
Approve/coach-call decision matches the reviewer on at least 90% of completed screens
p90 response latency no worse than the current stack's
Cost per completed screen no higher than the current stack's
